judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Qualtrics Site Intercept feedback tab: div#slider-control-SI_0B6adVoKRcC6ovz, a transparent overlay on the 'Feedback' tab, focusable, with click and keydown listeners, role generic and no name in the snapshot. Qualtrics' current SliderModule.js builds exactly this: a div with tabIndex=0 whose click and Enter/Space toggle the survey panel, with no role and no aria attributes. It is a real control (it opens and closes the panel) exposed with no role and no name, which is F59. The widget is injected by script, not in the static HTML, but the vendor code confirms the structure users get when the intercept shows; I found no capture difference that touches the claim.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Header search combobox, placeholder 'What can we help you find?'. The site's CSS (global.css) sets .form-control::placeholder{color:#6c757d;opacity:1}, and #6c757d on #ffffff is 4.69:1, above 4.5:1 for 13px text. The darkest rendered pixel of the placeholder in the screenshot is #717781 (4.51:1). #7fb6ea is a sub-pixel anti-aliasing fringe colour (it measures 2.15:1, not the 4.29:1 the message pairs it with), so the claim is wrong as worded and the text passes 1.4.3. Live CSS and markup match the capture. The rule had the pixels and chose a fringe colour as the text colour.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Hero photo link to the Gift Shop (/llb/shop/509870/). The link holds only the img, so its name is the alt 'Family gathered around a campfire in the woods, roasting marshmallows...'. Nothing in it says the link leads to the Gift Shop; the overlaid 'This Holiday, Give Presence' and 'HOLIDAY GIFT SHOP' are separate links in a sibling div, and 1.1.1 has no context provision. For an image that is the only content of a link, the alt has to describe the link's purpose (control clause of 1.1.1, H30), and this one only describes the scene. I looked for a technique that would rescue it (aria-label, title, hidden text, aria-hidden or tabindex=-1 on the link) and found none, on the live page either.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: Image-only link in the hero grid (no visible text); its name is the alt 'Small dog beside a green and cream canvas tote bag.', and the link leads to 'The Original Maine-Made Boat and Tote' (the file is Hero_Grid_Mini_Boat_and_Tote). The sentence is true of the capture: the image is all the link holds and the alt describes the photo, not the destination. But the alt names the product the destination sells (a canvas tote, though the dog comes first), and a sighted user gets no more than the photo of that product, so a user can infer the link's purpose from the name; my lean is that it meets 1.1.1. A strict reading of H30 and the WAI functional-image guidance (describe the destination, not the image) would fail it, so competent auditors would reasonably disagree: uncertain. The live HTML matches the snapshot.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: A frame div of the Qualtrics feedback tab (body > div:nth-of-type(9) > div:nth-of-type(5)), same bounds as the real toggle, focusable, keydown listener only, no click listener. Qualtrics' BuildElementModule gives every creative element tabIndex=0 and a keydown handler (clickOnKeyDown) that only calls click() on the element, and this one has no click handler, so Enter or Space does nothing: it does not work as a control. The control is the sibling slider-control overlay, judged separately. What this element adds is a pointless tab stop (a focus-order issue, not named by the claim), not a user interface component without a role. The rule took a keydown listener for a control.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Footer 'Sign Up for Email' field: input#foot-email type=text, aria-label 'Enter email address', no autocomplete attribute, both in the post-script snapshot and in the live server HTML. It collects the user's own email address, a purpose listed in 'Input Purposes for User Interface Components', so 1.3.5 needs autocomplete='email' (H98). type=text and the aria-label do not identify the purpose. I looked for a technique that would satisfy 1.3.5 here and found none.
